contexts.quote: Consider inactive and active conformations \(I,A\) with switching rates \(\alpha,\beta\). An exchange event occurs only from \(A\), at a constant effective hazard \(q\), and ends that molecule's first-event process. All rates have inverse-time units. Set \(s=\alpha+\beta\) and \(p=\alpha/s\). Ligand occupancy is held fixed; no ligand titration or baseline correction is represented. Substrate access and catalytic chemistry are collapsed into \(q\), with no substrate feedback or extra bound states. Initially the conformations have their unreacted equilibrium probabilities \((1-p,p)\).
contexts.where: “With fixed occupancy and no additional substrate-bound states, let \(J_{\mathrm{count}}\) denote stationary event flux for non-perturbing counting, \(J_{\mathrm{reset}}\) stationary event flux when each event resets the system to inactive, and \(T_{\mathrm{eq}}\) the mean waiting time to an absorbing first event starting from event-free equilibrium.”
